title: Panes move into the kit and hold content ids
body:
`panes.rs` holds the split tree, tabs, pane bars, drop zones and zoom, and each pane tab is a `Client` holding a smithay `ToplevelSurface`, its app id, pid and terminal-tab flag. Pinned panes wait on an app id. Hit testing and the drag state machine sit partly in `panes.rs` and partly in `compositor/input.rs`.

## Proposal

Panes move into the kit. A pane tab holds an opaque content id. decade keeps a map from id to its Wayland client and everything decade-specific about it: app id, pid, pinned app id, terminal tab, scratch mark and agent state. The kit lays out panes and emits their chrome plus a `Shape::Content { id, rect }` per visible content. decade's backend draws the client's surface there.

The kit takes pointer and key events in its own types and returns actions: focus a pane, resize, move, close, switch tab, or input for a content id at a pane-local point. decade forwards the last to the client.

## Open: what decade's Wayland handling needs from panes

Each of these works today and has to keep working. The review should check each one against the content-id design:

- configure: a client is told its size from its pane's rect, and again on every relayout
- hidden tabs: clients in a tab not shown get no frame callbacks
- keyboard focus follows the focused pane and its shown tab
- pinned panes: an empty pinned pane waits for a client with its app id
- pane tabs of terminals started by decade, matched by app id
- the drag ghost and the picker draw client surfaces scaled down
- popups and subsurfaces position relative to their toplevel's pane
- restore: a saved layout comes back with its panes before any client has connected

Also open: whether the kit's input types cover what `compositor/input.rs` does with modifiers and the Ctrl bar.

Blocked on the drawing seam, and on Jack's sign-off of the design.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/913b1d2c
notes.text: The remote viewer in decade-e3a784 is the kit's second user. A viewer on another machine runs the kit, draws the chrome locally, and receives each pane's content as streamed pixels for its content id. So the review of this design should check each Wayland behaviour above for where it runs when the viewer is remote. A second content kind, an app channel instead of pixels, is the parked idea in decade-b410e5.
